title: UPSC CSE - World Geography - World Climatic Regions
subject: World Geography

questions.q:
Consider the following description:
1. Annual and daily range of temperatures is low.
2. Precipitation occurs throughout the year.
3. Precipitation varies between 50 cm - 250 cm.

What is this type of climate?
questions.explain: Marine west coast climate is located poleward from the Mediterranean climate on the west coast of the continents. The main areas are: Northwestern Europe, west coast of North America, north of California, southern Chile, southeastern Australia and New Zealand.\n\nDue to marine influence, the temperature is moderate and in winter, it is warmer than for its latitude. The mean temperature in summer months ranges from 15°- 20°C and in winter 4°-10°C. The annual and daily ranges of temperature are small. Precipitation occurs throughout the year. Precipitation varies greatly from 50-250cm.

questions.q:
Consider the following States:
1. Arunachal Pradesh
2. Himachal Pradesh
3. Mizoram
In which of the above States do 'Tropical Wet Evergreen Forests' occur?
questions.explain: The Tropical Wet Evergreen Forests are found in the western slope of the Western Ghats, hills of the north-eastern region (Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Tripura, West Bengal) and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. They are found in warm and humid areas with annual precipitation of over 200 cm and mean annual temperature above 22°C.

questions.q: Each day is more or less the same, the morning is clear and bright with a sea breeze; as the Sun climbs high in the sky, heat mounts up, dark clouds form, then rain comes with thunder and lightning. But the rain is soon over. Which of the following regions is described in the above passage?
questions.explain: In the equatorial region, the annual rainfall is high as it rains almost every day. The temperatures are constant all year round – the temperature range is usually only a few degrees. There are no seasons. Each day is more or less the same, the morning is clear and bright with a sea breeze; as the Sun climbs high in the sky, heat mounts up, dark clouds form, then rain comes with thunder and lightning. But the rain is soon over.

questions.q: The seasonal reversal of winds is the typical characteristic of:
questions.explain: The seasonal reversal of winds is the typical characteristic of Monsoon climate. Monsoon climate is identified with a major wind system that seasonally reverses its direction—such as one that blows for approximately six months from the northeast and six months from the southwest. It can cause heavy rainfall during the summer and dry spells in the winter.

questions.q:
Which of the following leaf modifications occurs/occur in desert areas to inhibit water loss?
1. Hard and waxy leaves
2. Tiny leaves or no leaves
3. Thorns instead of leaves
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explain: Desert plants lose very little water through transpiration. The leaves in desert plants are either absent, very small, or they are present in the shape of spines. This helps in reducing loss of water from the leaves through transpiration. Plants growing in extreme dry conditions throughout the year adopted thorns instead of leaves to prevent loss of water.

questions.q: Climate is extreme, rainfall is scanty, and the people used to be nomadic herders. The above statement best describes which of the following regions?
questions.explain: A steppe is a dry, grassy plain. Steppes occur in temperate climates, which lie between the tropics and polar regions. Temperate regions have distinct seasonal temperature changes, with cold winters and warm summers. Climate is extreme, rainfall is scanty, and the people used to be nomadic herders is the best description of Steppe. The best-known pastoral and hunter-gatherer tribe in history were the Mongols. They inhabited the grasslands (steppes) of Central Asia.

questions.q:
Which of the following is/are unique characteristics / characteristics of equatorial forests?
1. Presence of tall, closely set trees with crowns forming a continuous canopy
2. Coexistence of a large number of species
3. Presence of numerous varieties of epiphytes
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explain: Equatorial forests are also called tropical rainforests. These thick forests occur in the regions near the equator and close to the tropics. These regions are hot and receive heavy rainfall throughout the year. As there is no particular dry season, the trees do not shed their leaves altogether. This is the reason they are called evergreen. All three characteristics mentioned are correct for equatorial forests.

questions.q: Which one of the following is the characteristic climate of the Tropical Savannah Region?
options: A definite dry and wet season
questions.explain: By distinct wet and dry seasons the Savanna climate is characterised by high temperature throughout the year (ranging between 24°C and 27°C), and abundant insolation. In any month of the year Temperature does not fall below 20°C. Savanna climate is similar to equatorial climate as regards temperature but the annual range of temperature ranging between 3°C and 8°C is greater than in the equatorial climate.

questions.q:
What could be the main reason/reasons for the formation of African and Eurasian desert belts?
1. It is located in the subtropical high-pressure cells.
2. It is under the influence of warm ocean currents.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct in this context?
questions.explain: The desert occurs in two broad belts viz. at 20-30° north and south of the Equator along the Tropics of Cancer and Capricorn. At the equator hot air would rise and spread north and south before cooling and it would condense and release its moisture over the tropical zones leading to development of an equatorial zone of low atmospheric pressure. The two tropical zones are at high pressure and nearer to the poles are two low-pressure belts of cold. As the denser air sinks towards the ground to the two subtropical high-pressure belts, wind is created which is hot and completely lacking in moisture. This blows across the Middle East, the Sahara, and North America. Eurasian Belt is related to cold currents not warm current.
